# Your money is frozen and I'm angry about it too

*Inês, Pinha · Tuesday, 10 November 2026*

I'm Inês. I design most of what you see in the Pinha app and I write most of the words in it. Rui, our CEO, would normally write this. He's been on calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal since early morning and will be for the rest of the day, so it's me.

If you've tried to take money out of Pinha since Friday, you already know something is very wrong. Here is what happened, what we're doing, and what you can do right now.

## What happened

Pinha doesn't hold your money ourselves. Like most small fintech apps, we work with a licensed payments partner. Ours is Northvale Payments, an e-money institution in Vilnius. Your savings sit in what's called a safeguarded account at Northvale. That account is kept separate from Northvale's own money, and Northvale isn't allowed to use it for its own business.

On Wednesday, 4 November, Northvale emailed us to end our contract with 30 days' notice. Their only explanation was a "risk appetite review." That's it. No specifics, no conversation.

Thirty days was going to be tight, but we could have moved everyone to a new partner without you noticing much.

Then on Friday, 6 November, at 09:00, Northvale blocked every outgoing transfer from Pinha. No warning, no call, nothing. This went directly against their own notice. Deposits and round-ups stopped at the same time. Since that morning nobody has been able to withdraw, including us on your behalf.

Our account manager at Northvale stopped answering our calls that same Friday. Their phone now goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian.

I'll say what I think. Giving 30 days' notice and then pulling the plug two days later isn't "risk management." It's cowardice. They didn't have the decency to stand behind their own letter, and 14,000 people are paying for it.

## Is my money safe?

Yes. It is not lost.

Your balance is still in the safeguarded account. Northvale can't spend it, lend it or mix it with their own money. Every euro of it is accounted for, and it's still yours.

But I won't dress this up. Safe is not the same as available. Until Northvale releases it, neither you nor we can move it, and for a lot of you that's the part that matters.

## What we're doing about it

**We've already signed a new partner.** Ostra Bank, based in Lisbon, will hold Pinha balances from now on. They're regulated here in Portugal, and we can walk into their office if we need to.

**To move your money to Ostra, two things have to happen.** Northvale has to send us the balances file, which is the official record of what each person holds. Banco de Portugal also has to approve the migration. We're pushing on both every day.

**Our best estimate right now is 10 to 15 working days.** Please read that as an estimate, not a promise. Most of it depends on Northvale, and Northvale has already shown us what their word is worth this week. I'm not going to give you a date and then come back and move it. If the estimate changes, for better or worse, you'll hear it from us.

**We've filed formal complaints.** On Saturday, 7 November, we complained to Banco de Portugal and to the Bank of Lithuania, which supervises Northvale. A licensed institution blocking safeguarded customer funds against its own contractual notice is something regulators need to look at, and we've asked them to.

**We're trying to get money out early for people in urgent situations.** More on that below.

## What you can do right now

**1. If you're in an urgent situation, email urgent@pinha.example and put URGENTE in the subject line.** By urgent I mean rent, medical costs, losing your job, or anything else where waiting weeks does real damage. Tell us briefly what's going on. We're going to Northvale with these cases one by one and asking for individual releases. I can't promise they'll agree, but we're asking, and every real case we bring them makes it harder for them to say no.

**2. For everything else, our normal support email still works, but please be patient with us.** We've received about 1,900 emails since Friday. Three people are answering them. Right now a reply takes around two days. Every email is read by a person, and we're not using automated replies to make the queue look shorter.

**3. You don't need to do anything to keep your money safe.** You don't need to close your account or send us documents. When the migration to Ostra happens, your balance moves with you. If we ever need something from you, it will come through the app and this blog, never through a random link in an SMS.

**4. You won't pay a fee for November or December.** We've cancelled the monthly fee for everyone for both months. It's a small thing next to what this is costing some of you, and I know that. But charging you for a service that isn't working would be indecent.

**5. Check here for updates.** We'll post on this blog every Monday and Thursday until this is fully solved, even if all we can say is "nothing moved." The next update is Thursday, 12 November.

## Our part in this

I don't want this post to only point at Northvale, because some of this is on us.

We had one partner and no backup. When things were going well, a second partner felt like something we'd sort out "later," when we were bigger. That was naive. If we'd had a second provider ready, Friday would have been a bad day for us instead of a crisis for you. We didn't, and that's our mistake. We're fixing it, and Ostra is the start, but that doesn't help anyone who needs their money this week.

I designed the screen in the app that says "your money is always yours, take it out anytime." I've looked at it a lot since Friday and it makes me feel sick. The money is still yours. "Anytime" turned out not to be true, and my name is on that line too.

## One message

On Sunday, on the metro, I read an email from a woman in Porto, written entirely in capitals. She's been saving for three years for the deposit on a car. The dealer has given her until Friday to pay. I nearly cried in the carriage, and I'm not embarrassed to say it.

Her case is in the urgent queue, along with everyone else who's written in with a deadline they can't move. I'm telling you about her because she isn't a ticket number to us, and neither are you.

## You're allowed to be angry

You're allowed to be angry at Northvale, and you're allowed to be angry at us. I'm not going to ask anyone to stay calm. If you trusted us with three years of round-ups and now you can't touch them, anger is the right reaction.

Here's what I can promise, because these are the only things fully in our hands. We'll tell you the truth, including when it's bad news. We'll post every Monday and Thursday. We won't give you a fake date. And we won't stop until every euro is back where you can reach it.

If you need your money urgently: **urgent@pinha.example, subject URGENTE.**

Next update: Thursday, 12 November.

— Inês

---

A few things to check before it goes up:

- **Ask Rui or the lawyers to look at the Northvale section.** I kept "cowardice" because it's how you feel and it reads honest. But it's an accusation against a company you're in a legal fight with. Getting a quick yes from them is safer than finding out afterwards that it caused problems.
- **The Porto story.** I left out her name and anything that could identify her beyond the city. It would still be kind to ask her if she's okay being mentioned, since she might recognise herself.
- **The 10–15 working days.** Your notes don't say when that count starts. I kept it vague ("our best estimate right now"). If it actually means "after Northvale sends the file," it's worth saying so.
- **Dates.** You said it publishes Tuesday 10 November, but today is the 11th. If it's going out today, change the date at the top. The Thursday 12 November update still works either way.
